interest: Shows early US planning for Taiwan's postwar status: Kerr's 1943 outline, naming questions, and the 1944 sovereignty-versus-military-administration debate.
overview: This file contains U.S. State Department records dating from February 1942 to June 1944 concerning Formosa (Taiwan) under Japanese colonial rule and planning for its wartime and post-war status. The documents reflect the evolution of American policy from initial strategic assessments and intelligence compilation—notably a substantial 1942 study on Japanese administration and a comprehensive 33-page historical chronology compiled by George H. Kerr of the Military Intelligence Service—to practical diplomatic and legal considerations in 1944. These later records trace exchanges between Washington and the U.S. Embassy in Chungking to determine official Chinese preferences regarding English nomenclature ('Taiwan' versus 'Formosa'), as well as crucial legal deliberations on defining sovereignty, post-war U.S. military government authority, and the timing of the island's eventual transfer from Japan to China.
